status: PROPOSAL — not ground truth. Provenance is #llm throughout: no glyph
status_cont: identity here is adopted, and every Tier-1 form awaits ratification.

contamination.why: This page is NOT a blind sample and must not be counted as one. Its TEI body was read openly in an earlier session and is committed at tei/chukchi-1-151.xml; the four Tier-1 forms below agree with it because I had seen it, not because two witnesses concur. CLAUDE.md lists 1-151 among the four spent refs.
contamination.consequence: Use this page to exercise the loop, never to measure reading accuracy.

notes: ALTO order is not reading order on this page. Line 0 is the chapter head at
vpos 896, line 9 the section head at 1030, and line 1 the first body line at
1130 — so 9 belongs between 0 and 1. Lines 19-32 are the narrow measure beside
the figure, 35-36 the footnote, 37-38 the figure caption, 39 the folio. The
restore is keyed by line id and is order-independent, but do not read the
index sequence as the text's sequence.
Small caps flattened to full caps, following the only precedent in surviving
GT (1-074's running title): line 1 SEAL-HUNTING, line 9 HUNTING AND FISHING.
Curly quotes reproduced as printed (Tier-1-scoped ASCII policy, keying spec 1).
Line 27 has ink at its right edge that is not text on this line — bleed from
the figure block at hpos 1552. Not keyed.

0.note: chapter head; em dash as printed

1.text: SEAL-HUNTING. — The Maritime Chukchee support themselves almost
1.note: SEAL-HUNTING set in small caps, flattened

2.text: exclusively by hunting sea-mammals, the most important among which are the

3.text: following species of seal: Phoca hispida (English, “ringed or rough seal;”

4.text: Russian Siberian, акипка; Chukchee, mêˊmêl), Phoca ochotensis macrodens1
4.resolved: mêˊmêl = m + e+U+0302, U+02CA, m + e+U+0302, l. Both circumflexes confirmed at 3x.
4.note: акипка confirmed letter by letter at 3x — а к и п к а, six sorts, no pre-reform character. Trailing 1 is the footnote marker (superscript), keyed as a bare digit here; the ALTO carries no markup and note-anchoring is a collation concern.

5.text: (Russian Siberian, ларга; Chukchee, keliˊlɪn [“the spotted one”]), Histriophoca
5.resolved: keliˊlɪn: the i after kel carries its dot; the sort after the second l does not and is x-height — U+026A. Confirmed at 3x.

6.text: fasciata (English, “ribbon-seal;” Russian Siberian, крылатая нерпа [winged seal];

7.text: Chukchee, veˊhɪl-keliˊlɪn), and Erignathus barbatus (English, “ground-seal” or
7.resolved: veˊhɪl-keliˊlɪn: dotless x-height sort after h and after the second l, both U+026A. Hyphen is U+002D, the Tier-1 connector — not a line-break artifact, it is mid-line.

8.resolved: uˊᵋnel = u, U+02CA, U+1D4B (raised small epsilon), n, e, l.
8.note: лахтакъ ends in a PRE-REFORM WORD-FINAL HARD SIGN, U+044A (keying spec 2.7). Keyed as printed. The committed TEI has лахтак, modernized — licensed there, since the word is glossed 'ground-seal'/'thong-seal', but ground truth reproduces the print. Confirmed at 3x: the final sort has the ascender of ъ, not the bowl-only ь.

9.note: section head, small caps flattened; sits between lines 0 and 1 on the page

10.text: The seals are killed with harpoons, shot with fire-arms, or caught in nets,

11.text: according to their mode of life in the different seasons. The varieties of

12.text: harpoons used by the Chukchee in seal-hunting differ mainly in the length of

13.text: the shaft and the size of the point. Short, light harpoons are used chiefly in

14.text: winter in killing the animals through their blow-holes. Long-shafted harpoons

15.text: are used in spring to stalk the animals on the smooth ice, and also during the

16.text: summer on the open water. Now, however, this latter style of harpoon has

17.text: been almost superseded by the gun in this kind of hunting. The form of the

18.text: head is more or less uniform, while there are two different ways of attaching

19.text: the head to the shaft, the method being the same

20.text: for short as for long harpoons. The head of the

21.text: Chukchee harpoon is cut out of bone, ivory, or antler.

22.text: It is from three to four inches long, and has a piece

23.text: of iron inserted in a slit at the top. I obtained one

24.text: harpoon-head the body of which is made of brass,

25.text: with the usual slit for inserting the iron piece. Two

26.text: varieties of blade are used. One, found chiefly in the

27.text: smaller heads, has a lanceolate form, with lower

28.text: ends curved and filed off almost close to the body

29.text: of the head (Fig. 30, a); the other form is broader,
29.note: the a is italic, a figure-part letter

30.text: with lower ends protruding on both sides in sharp,

31.text: cutting angles (Fig. 30, b). These two styles of
31.note: italic b, matching line 29's a. CATMuS reads 6 here — italic b in this face has a closed bowl and a straight ascender that resembles a 6. It is b: the caption on line 37 lists parts a and b, and the LoI entry for fig. 30 has two segments.

32.text: blade correspond probably to two distinct forms of

33.text: stone or slate harpoon-points, which were used before the iron ones (Fig. 31).

34.text: The iron blade is firmly fastened into its slit with a wooden, bone, or iron peg.

35.text: 1 Similar, on account of its spotted skin, to the “harbor-seal,” but identified by Professor Allen as a new
35.note: footnote; leading 1 is the superscript marker, keyed as a bare digit

36.text: sub-species of Phoca ochotensis of Pallas.

37.note: figure caption, line 1 of 2. Taken verbatim from data/readings.md 1-151|d2082379, the editor's hand reading — the authoritative store for caption text. Catalogue numbers are the literal (??/????) per keying spec 2.8: deferred to a pass that can query the AMNH catalogue, not read off the raster. Recording what the raster shows so the deferral is auditable and not mistaken for illegibility: the editor reads 70/7867 and 70/7749 on the full page; the line crop clips the denominators and yields 1887/1749, which is why this is not a transcription task.

instrument.finding: PAD_BOTTOM = 18 clips a stacked fraction's denominator. Line 37's crop cut through both catalogue numbers, and the clipped digits read as 1887/1749 against 7867/7749 on the full raster — a plausible wrong reading with no signal that anything was missing, which is the same failure class as the PAD_Y=4 dot-below-g on 1-074.
instrument.not_fixed: Padding not changed. Raising it corpus-wide to fit a two-deck fraction would bleed a neighbouring line into every ordinary crop, and 2-030's 21 px pitch is the constraint. The affected content is exactly the catalogue numbers, which keying spec 2.8 now defers, so the clip costs nothing where it occurs.
instrument.for_the_loop: Worth knowing that a crop can silently omit material below the line box in either direction. Where a line carries anything two-deck — fractions, stacked figure letters — go to the raster.
